title: FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985
text:
FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 1  

 Short title 

 This Act may be cited as the Films and Censorship Act 1985.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 2  

 Interpretation 

 In this Act unless the context otherwise requires: 

 censor 

 includes the Chief Censor 

 document 

 means any book, newspaper, periodical, photograph, photographic slide or film, and any print or writing 

 exhibitor 

 , in relation to films, means any person who exhibits or causes to be exhibited any film to the public, and exhibit and exhibition have corresponding meanings 

 exhibitors licence 

 means an exhibitors licence granted pursuant to section 5 

 film 

 means any cinematographic film, and includes a video tape, DVD, (being a Digital VideoDisc or Digital Versatile Disc or an optical digital disc for storing movies and data), and any other article that contains a record of a visual moving image that is capable of being used for the subsequent projection of those images in a fixed sequence on to any screen, surface or media; and also includes any part of any such film and any copy or part of a copy of the whole or part of a film 

 indecent 

 includes describing, depicting, expressing or otherwise dealing with matters of sex, horror, crime, cruelty, or violence in a manner that is injurious to the public good 

 Inspector 

 means a person appointed in writing by the censor pursuant to section 15A 

 Minister 

 means the Minister responsible for the Crown Law Office 

 premises 

 means any building, enclosure, ground, or open-air space 

 prescribed 

 means prescribed by regulation 

 renter 

 means any person who supplies film for financial reward or other consideration and rent and renting have corresponding meanings 

 renter’s licence 

 means a renter’s licence granted pursuant to section 4. 

 [Section 2 film: replaced,18 April 2008, by section 2(2) of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .] 

 [Section 2 Inspector: inserted,18 April 2008, by section 2(1) of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 3  

 Licensing authority 

 The Minister or such officer as may be authorised by the Minister by notice in the Gazette is responsible for the issue of licences in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 4  

 Renter’s licence 

 (1)  

 No person may rent or cause or permit to be rented, any film unless he or she is the holder of a renter’s licence. 

 (2)  

 Any person who contravenes the provisions of subsection (1) is guilty of an offence and upon conviction is liable to a fine not exceeding $5,000. 

 [Section 4(2): amended, on 18 April 2008, by section 7 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 5  

 Exhibitor’s licence 

 (1)  

 No person may exhibit or cause or permit or suffer to be exhibited any film unless he or she is the holder of an exhibitor’s licence. 

 (2)  

 Any person who exhibits a film in contravention of the provisions of subsection (1) is guilty of an offence and upon conviction is liable to a fine not exceeding $5,000. 

 [Section 5(2): amended, on 18 April 2008, by section 7 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 6  

 Duties of exhibitors 

 Every holder of an exhibitor’s licence must ensure that every exhibition is conducted in such a manner as to provide for the safety, convenience and good order of the persons attending thereat and that there is a responsible and competent person operating the equipment used in the premises for the purpose of the exhibition.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 7  

 Exemptions 

 Films may be exhibited without an exhibitor’s licence— 

 (a) 

 by any charitable, philanthropic, religious, educational, social or sporting body or organisation where— 

 (i) 

 the film is exhibited to further the bona fide objects or purpose of the body or organisation, those objects or purposes being other than the exhibiting of film; and 

 (ii) 

 admission to the exhibition is restricted to the members of that body or organisation and their families; and 

 (iii) 

 after meeting actual expenses and charges incurred in that exhibition, any proceeds derived from the exhibition are applied solely and entirely towards the funds of the body of organisation so exhibiting the film, and no portion of those proceeds is payable to any person by way of fee, commission, or other financial reward for acts performed or services rendered by that person in arranging, providing, or carrying out the exhibition except any fee payable to any person projecting the film: 

 (b) 

 in any hotel premises which are the subject of a licence issued under the provisions of the Tourist Authority Act 1968 where the exhibition is for the benefit of hotel guests only.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 8  

 Applications 

 (1)  

 Every application for a licence under this Act must be made to the Minister or such officer as may be authorised pursuant to section 3 and must be made in such form and manner and must contain, or be accompanied by, such information, and documents as may be prescribed. 

 (2)  

 Where an application is made in accordance with subsection (1) and is accompanied by the prescribed fee the Minister or duly authorised officer may if he or she is satisfied that the applicant— 

 (a) 

 is capable of complying with such conditions as may be imposed or attached to the licence; and 

 (b) 

 is in all other respects a suitable person to be granted a licence— 

 issue subject to such conditions as he or she may impose or as may be attached thereto, a licence in such form as may be prescribed to the applicant in respect of the premises for which the application was made. 

 (3)  

 The Minister may by instrument in writing, vary or revoke at any time any condition for the time being attached to the licence pursuant to subsection (2).

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 9  

 Duration and renewal 

 Unless cancelled under section 10, a licence remains in force for 1 year and may be renewed from time to time.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 10  

 Cancellation of licence 

 The Minister may cancel or suspend any licence where the licensee— 

 (a) 

 breaches any condition attached to his or her licence pursuant to section 8; or 

 (b) 

 is convicted of an offence under the Copyright Act 1962; or 

 (c) 

 is convicted of an offence under this Part.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 11  

 Appeals against refusal, variation, suspension, or cancellation of licence 

 (1)  

 Where— 

 (a) 

 an applicant is refused a licence; or 

 (b) 

 a licence is cancelled or suspended; or 

 (c) 

 conditions imposed or attaching to a licence are varied, 

 the applicant or the licensee, as the case may be, may within 14 days appeal to the High Court against such refusal, cancellation, suspension or variation. 

 (2)  

 The decision of the High Court under this section is final.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 12  

 Transfer of licenses 

 Every licence issued under this Act is only valid in respect of the premises for which it is granted and is not transferable without the consent of the Minister or a duly authorised officer.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 13  

 Lost licence 

 Any licensee whose licence has been lost or destroyed may on payment of the prescribed fee obtain a duplicate licence from the person by which the original licence was issued.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 1  LICENCES 

 14  

 Licences to be displayed 

 Every licensee must display and keep displayed in a prominent place at the premises in respect of which a licence is issued, a current licence.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 2  CENSORSHIP OF FILMS AND DOCUMENTS 

 15  

 Appointment of censors 

 The Minister may from time to time appoint a fit and proper person to be the Chief Censor of films and documents and such other censors and officers as may be required for the purposes of this Act.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 2  CENSORSHIP OF FILMS AND DOCUMENTS 

 15A  

 Appointment of Inspectors 

 (1)  

 The censor may appoint any fit and proper person to be an Inspector to assist the censor in the carrying out of his or her functions under this Act. 

 (2)  

 The censor may in writing delegate to an Inspector all or any of his or her powers or functions except this power of delegation. 

 [Section 15A: inserted, on18 April 2008, by section 3 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 16  

 Films to be approved by censor before exhibition 

 No person may exhibit any film other than a film exempted under the provisions of section 20 from the operation of this Part, unless and until such film has been approved by the censor for public exhibition.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 17  

 Offence to exhibit film not approved by censor 

 (1)  

 Every person who in any place to which the public are admitted, exhibits or is concerned in the exhibition of any film or part of a film which— 

 (a) 

 has not been approved by the censor; or 

 (b) 

 is being shown in breach of any condition imposed by the censor, 

 commits an offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding $5,000 in respect of every occasion on which such film or any parts thereof have been so exhibited. 

 (2)  

 Any film in respect of which an offence under this Act has been committed may by order of the convicting court made in addition to any other penalty, be forfeited and thereafter may be destroyed or otherwise dealt with as the Minister may direct. 

 [Section 17(1): amended, on 18 April 2008, by section 7 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 18  

 Duties of censors 

 (1)  

 It is the duty of the censor to examine every film duly submitted to him or her for examination with a view to such film being approved for purposes of exhibition to the public. 

 (2)  

 On the completion of the examination of any film the censor may— 

 (a) 

 approve the showing for exhibition: 

 (b) 

 refuse to approve the same: 

 (c) 

 agree to approve the same subject to such excisions from the film he or she thinks proper. 

 (3)  

 The approval by the censor must not be given with respect to any film or to any part of a film which in his or her opinion depicts any matter which is contrary to public order or is indecent or the exhibition of which would for any other reason be undesirable in the public interest. 

 (4)  

 Such approval may be for general exhibition, or may be given subject to a condition that the film should be exhibited only to any specified class or classes of persons, or may be given subject to any other conditions whatsoever that the censor in the public interest thinks fit to impose.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 19  

 Fees 

 There is payable to the censor such fees in respect of the examination of films as may be prescribed.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 20  

 Exemption from censorship 

 (1)  

 The censor, may on application made to him or her, waive compliance by any person, organisation, or body, either unconditionally or subject to such conditions as the censor thinks fit, with the requirements of this Part in respect of any films of any of the following classes— 

 (a) 

 films used for educational and instructional purposes: 

 (b) 

 films directly related to the curriculum of primary, secondary or tertiary educational institutions: 

 (c) 

 films wholly or mainly of a religious nature: 

 (d) 

 films that are wholly or mainly commercial advertisements relating to the advertisers’ or sponsors’ activities: 

 (e) 

 films relating wholly or mainly to the social sciences, including economics, geography, anthropology, and linguistics: 

 (f) 

 films depicting wholly or mainly cultural activities. 

 (2)  

 The censor must not grant a waiver under subsection (1) in respect of any particular film or any particular class of films if he or she has any reason to believe that the exhibition of that film or films of that class is likely to be injurious to the public good. 

 (3)  

 The censor may at any time revoke any waiver granted under subsection (1), either wholly or in part. 

 (4)  

 Notwithstanding that the censor has granted a waiver to any person, body or organisation in respect of any film or class of films under subsection (1) the censor may require that person, body or organisation to submit that film or any particular film of that class to him or her under this Part, in which case the provisions of this Part apply accordingly.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 21  

 Examination of films by censor 

 In determining whether the exhibition of any film is or is not likely to be undesirable in the public interest, or is or is not contrary to public order, or is not indecent, the censor must consider the following matters— 

 (a) 

 the dominant effect of the film as a whole: 

 (b) 

 the extent to which the film has merit, value or importance in relation to artistic, social, cultural or other matters: 

 (c) 

 the extent and degree to which, or the manner in which, the film depicts, includes, or treats anti-social behaviour, cruelty, violence, crime, sex, or indecent or offensive language or behaviour: 

 (d) 

 the extent and degree to which and the manner in which the film denigrates any particular class of the general public by reference to the colour, race, or ethnic or national origins, the sex, or the religious beliefs or the members of that class: 

 (e) 

 any other relevant circumstances relating to the proposed exhibition of the film, including the places and times at which, or the occasion on which, the film is intended or likely to be exhibited.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 22  

 Censor may consult other persons 

 In examining any film for the purpose of this Act, the censor may exhibit the film to any person whom the censor considers may be able to assist them in forming an opinion of the film on which to base their decision in respect of the film.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 23  

 Special provisions relating to film sold or rented to public 

 (1)  

 No person may sell to the public or rent to the public, or offer or expose for sale or renting to the public, any film (not being blank film), unless the film has been approved by a censor for sale or renting to the public, and any conditions imposed by the censor in granting his or her approval are complied with. 

 (2)  

 Subject to subsection (4), nothing in subsection (1) applies with respect to any film imported into the Cook Islands before the commencement of this section. 

 (3)  

 Every person carrying on at the commencement of this section the business of selling or renting film to the public must, within 14 days after the commencement of this section, supply to the censor a list specifying— 

 (a) 

 the titles of all film in his or her possession for sale or renting that were imported into the Cook Islands before the commencement of this section; and 

 (b) 

 the number of copies of each film specified in the list held by him or her. 

 (4)  

 The censor may, by notice in writing to the person supplying such a list, direct that he or she must not sell or rent or offer or expose for sale or rent, any film specified in the list, unless it is approved by the censor for sale or renting and is in compliance with any conditions imposed by the censor in granting that approval. 

 (5)  

 The foregoing provisions of this Part as far as they are applicable and with the necessary modifications, apply with respect to every film required to be approved by the censor pursuant to this section as if the film was film intended for exhibition. 

 [Section 23 heading: amended,18 April 2008, by section 4 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .] 

 [Section 23: amended,18 April 2008, by section 4 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 24  

 Duties of licencees 

 (1)  

 Every licencee must set up and maintain a register of all films kept by him or her for rent or exhibition as the case may be. 

 (2)  

 The register must record the following particulars— 

 (a) 

 the title of the film; and 

 (b) 

 the number of copies (if more than 1); and 

 (c) 

 the classification of the censor; or 

 as the case may be, any exemption granted; and 

 (d) 

 the date of the censor’s decision. 

 (3)  

 Every licencee must ensure that every film owned, rented, or exhibited by him or her clearly displays, at all times, the classification of the censor, or, as the case may be, the exemption granted.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 25  

 Offences and penalties 

 (1)  

 Every person commits an offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding $5,000, who being the holder of a renter’s licence, rents any film otherwise than in accordance with section 23. 

 [Section 25(1): amended, on 18 April 2008, by section 7 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 26  

 Register of films 

 (1)  

 For the purpose of this Act, the censor must set up and maintain a register of films, recording the following particulars— 

 (a) 

 the title of the film; and 

 (b) 

 the name of the person applying under section 16 or 23 for approval of the film, or as the case may be, under section 20 for exemption of the film from censorship; and 

 (c) 

 the number of copies of the film brought into the Cook Islands; and 

 (d) 

 the classification approved by the censor or, as the case may be, any exemption granted, and the date of the censor’s decision; and 

 (e) 

 where he or she has approved or exempted the film subject to any conditions, particulars of those conditions; and 

 (f) 

 where he or she has refused to approve the film for exhibition or has approved the film for exhibition following the making of any excisions or alterations, the reason for that decision. 

 (2)  

 The register of films must otherwise be in such form as the censor thinks fit. 

 (3)  

 The register of films must be open to inspection by the public, without fee, during ordinary office hours.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 FILMS 

 27  

 Constable, censor or Inspector powers of entry 

 (1)  

 Every constable, censor or Inspector may enter any premises (not being a private dwelling house) in which film is being exhibited or in which he or she has reason to believe that film is being exhibited, or acting on the instructions of the constable, censor or Inspector, for the purpose of ensuring that the provisions of this Act are being complied with. 

 (2)  

 In the exercise of the powers conferred by subsection (1), a constable, censor or Inspector may require the production for his or her inspection of any licence or certificate issued under this Act and may require the holder to give such information as the constable, censor or Inspector may reasonably require for the proper performance of his or her duties. 

 (3)  

 Without limiting the foregoing provisions of this section, every constable, censor or Inspector who discovers any person— 

 (a) 

 exhibiting any film that has not been approved for exhibition by the constable, censor or Inspector; or 

 (b) 

 exhibiting any film in breach of any condition imposed by the constable, censor or Inspector: 

 (c) 

 not being the holder of an exhibitor’s or renter’s licence exhibits or rents any film in breach of any provision of this Act, 

 may seize the film and deliver it to the constable, censor or Inspector. 

 (4)  

 The constable, censor or Inspector may, at their discretion, retain any film delivered to him or her under subsection (3) for subsequent disposal or destruction as he or she thinks fit. 

 (5)  

 Every person commits an offence, and is liable to a fine not exceeding $5,000, who obstructs any constable, censor or Inspector in the performance of their duties under this section or who fails to comply with any requirements of a constable, censor or Inspector under subsection (2). 

 [Section 27 heading: amended, on18 April 2008, by section 5 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .] 

 [Section 27: amended, on18 April 2008, by section 5 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .] 

 [Section 27(5): amended, on18 April 2008, by section 7 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 DOCUMENTS 

 28  

 Functions of censor 

 The functions of the censor in relation to documents or sound recordings are— 

 (a) 

 to determine the character of any document or sound recording submitted to him or her for classification: 

 (b) 

 to classify documents or sound recordings submitted to him or her as indecent or not indecent or as indecent in the hands of persons under a specified age or as indecent unless their circulation is restricted to specified persons or classes of persons or unless used for a particular purpose, as the case may be: 

 (c) 

 to hear and determine any questions relating to the character of a book or sound recording referred to him or her by a court in any civil or criminal proceedings whether under this Act or otherwise, and to forward a report of its findings to that court: 

 (d) 

 to determine whether a film is a counterfeit or pirate copy produced without or not bearing the appropriate authorisation of the copyright, patent or authorised holder and therefore violating a copyright, patent or a protection complementary certificate: 

 (e) 

 to seize and destroy any such film as described in paragraph (d). 

 [Section 28(d): inserted, on18 August 2008, by section 6 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .] 

 [Section 28(e): inserted, on18 August 2008, by section 6 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 DOCUMENTS 

 29  

 Matters to be taken into account by censor 

 (1)  

 In classifying or determining the character of any document or sound recording the censor must take into consideration— 

 (a) 

 the dominant effect of the document or sound recording: 

 (b) 

 the person, classes of persons, or age groups to or among whom the document or sound recording is or is intended or is likely to be published, heard, distributed, sold, exhibited, played, given, sent, or delivered: 

 (c) 

 the literary or artistic merit, or the medical, legal, political, social or scientific character or importance of the document or sound recording: 

 (d) 

 the price at which the book or sound recording sells or is intended to be sold: 

 (e) 

 whether any person is likely to be corrupted by reading the book or hearing the sound recording and whether other persons are likely to benefit therefrom: 

 (f) 

 whether the document or the sound recording displays an honest purpose and an honest thread of thought or whether its content is merely camouflage designed to render acceptable any indecent parts of the document or sound recording. 

 (2)  

 Despite the provisions of subsection (1) where the publication of any document or the distribution of any sound recording would be in the interests of art, literature, science, or learning and would be for the public good, the censor must not classify it as indecent.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 DOCUMENTS 

 30  

 Submission of documents and sound recording to censor 

 (1)  

 The comptroller of customs or any other person may submit any document or sound recording to the censor for a decision as to whether or not it is indecent or for a decision as to its classification. 

 (2)  

 Any person whom the censor is satisfied is likely to be affected by the determination may make representations, orally or in writing, to the censor, and may call evidence.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 DOCUMENTS 

 31  

 Fees 

 Every submission to the censor must be accompanied by the prescribed fee.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 DOCUMENTS 

 32  

 Offences 

 (1)  

 Every person commits an offence against this Act who— 

 (a) 

 sells, or delivers by way of hire, or offers for sale or hire, or has in his or her possession for sale or hire, any indecent document or sound recording: 

 (b) 

 sells, delivers, gives, exhibits, or offers to any person under the age of 18 years, any document or sound recording which is indecent. 

 (2)  

 Every person who commits an offence against this section is liable to a fine not exceeding $5,000. 

 [Section 32(2): amended, on 18 April 2008, by section 7 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 3  MISCELLANEOUS 

 33  

 Importation prohibited 

 The importation of any indecent film or document is hereby declared to be prohibited, within the meaning of the Customs Revenue and Border Protection Act 2012. 

 [Section 33: amended, on1 August 2012, by Schedule 4 of the Customs Revenue and Border Protection Act 2012 (2012 No 5) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 3  MISCELLANEOUS 

 34  

 Offences 

 Any person who contravenes or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this Act for which no penalty is specifically provided is liable to a fine not exceeding $5,000. 

 [Section 34: amended, on 18 April 2008, by section 7 of the Films and Censorship Amendment Act 2008 (2008 No 6) .]

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 3  MISCELLANEOUS 

 35  

 Regulations 

 The Queen’s Representative may by Order in Executive Council prescribe all matters that are necessary for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 3  MISCELLANEOUS 

 36  

 Repeals 

 (1)  

 The Cinematograph Ordinance 1957 is hereby repealed. 

 (2)  

 The Customs Import Prohibition (Indecent Documents) Order 1980 is hereby revoked.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP ACT 1985 

 PART 3  MISCELLANEOUS 

 37  

 Transitional 

 Despite sections 4 and 5, a person who immediately before the date of commencement of this Act was a film renter or film exhibitor is entitled to continue to rent or exhibit as the case may be without a licence under this Act— 

 (a) 

 for a period of 90 days beginning with that date; or 

 (b) 

 if before the expiration of that period he or she shall apply for a licence under this Act, until that licence is granted or finally refused or the application is withdrawn.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP REGULATIONS 1986 

 FILMS AND CENSORSHIP REGULATIONS 1986

 Title

 Licence

 Every application for a renter’s licence must be accompanied by a fee of $50.

 The fee for a duplicate of a licence is $50.

 Licences 

 (1)  

 A renter’s licence must be in Form 3 in Schedule 1. 

 (2)  

 An exhibitor’s licence must be in Form 4 in Schedule 1.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP (FEES) ORDER 1987 

 1  

 Title and commencement 

 This order may be cited as the Films and Censorship (Fees) Order 1987 and comes into force on 1 January 1988.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP (FEES) ORDER 1987 

 2  

 Licence fees 

 The fees payable annually to the censor for the issue of a renter’s licence and for an exhibitor’s licence are as set out in the Schedule.

FILMS AND CENSORSHIP (FEES) ORDER 1987 

 3  

 Examination fees 

 The fees payable to the censor for the examination by the censor of video tapes, cinematographic film, documents and sound tapes are as set out in the Schedule.
